lines.text: Mempire is a real-time, one-versus-one card battler, where Bitcoin, memecoins and stocks fight in the arena, and the market decides who is strong today.
Price moves become small, bounded buffs and nerfs, written on chain by a Chainlink workflow.
Two players stake, battle for three minutes, and every card they drop is a Monad transaction.
That only works on a chain this fast. So we built it on Monad.
This is the live app on Monad testnet. That strip is Monad itself: each block voted in about three hundred milliseconds, and final in under six hundred, measured in this browser.
One tap as a guest. The relayer mints an eight-card starter deck, sends test AUSD, and a little MON for gas. About ten seconds. No wallet, no faucet.
The side boards show the market meta: who is buffed, who is nerfed, and how old the snapshot is. We pick the one-dollar tier in MON, and both players queue a ranked match.
Now every card I drop is its own transaction, signed by a per-match session key, so there are no popups. Each pill shows the real round trip: executed, then final.
When the second player's claim lands, the contract settles the pot: ninety percent to the winner, ten to the house.
Empire reads Monad's native staking precompile live, and checks passkey signatures with the P-256 precompile. New players can even open chests gaslessly, through EIP-7702 and our own paymaster.
Clans, and clan wars, score only the staked wins the relay has verified on chain. These clans were seeded by our team for the demo.
Mempire. Every coin is a fighter. Play it now at mempire-monad dot vercel dot app.
